accepted.s: The Composite Dialogue between India and Pakistan was originally agreed upon in which year?
accepted.x: The Composite Dialogue was agreed upon in 1997 and resumed in 2004 before being broken off after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.
accepted.tq: Use the direct date-recall approach for a bilateral diplomatic initiative.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the eight baskets of the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue?
o: Peace and security and confidence-building measures
accepted.x: The eight baskets included peace and security/CBMs, J&K, Siachen, Wullar Barrage/Tulbul, Sir Creek, terrorism and drugs, economic cooperation, and friendly exchanges. Nuclear disarmament was not listed as a basket.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the officially enumerated set.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Composite Dialogue between India and Pakistan:
1. It was resumed in 2004.
2. It was broken off after the Mumbai attacks of 26/11.
3. Its breakdowns were associated with the issue of terrorism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Composite Dialogue resumed in 2004, was suspended after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, and repeatedly broke down because of terrorism-related concerns.
accepted.tq: Combine a date, a turning point and a cause-effect relationship in one statement question.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to India-Pakistan relations, consider the following statements:
1. Backchannel diplomacy operated alongside formal diplomatic processes.
2. Such diplomacy was visible in the period preceding the 2021 ceasefire reaffirmation.
3. Backchannel diplomacy completely replaced official dialogue after 26/11.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Backchannel diplomacy ran alongside formal processes and was evident before the 2021 ceasefire reaffirmation. It did not completely replace official dialogue after 26/11.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word 'completely' while retaining the two supported statements.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: Sir Creek is best described as a:
o: 96-kilometre freshwater river between Punjab and Sindh
96-kilometre tidal estuary between Gujarat and Sindh
154-kilometre mountain pass between Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan
60-kilometre coastal canal between Rajasthan and Sindh
accepted.x: Sir Creek is a 96-kilometre tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch between Gujarat and Sindh.
accepted.tq: Link the geographical description with the distinctive numerical figure.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: The principal issue in the Sir Creek dispute concerns the:
o: Boundary line between India and Pakistan
Construction of a dam across the estuary
accepted.x: The Sir Creek dispute concerns the boundary line. Pakistan refers to the 1914 map line, whereas India advocates the mid-channel thalweg rule.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the boundary-line dispute from other possible maritime and resource issues.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the differing positions of India and Pakistan regarding the Sir Creek boundary?
o: India supports the 1914 map line, while Pakistan supports the thalweg rule.
Pakistan supports the mid-channel thalweg rule, while India rejects any boundary line.
Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India supports the mid-channel thalweg rule.
Both countries support the 1914 map line but differ over its historical date.
accepted.x: Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India relies on the mid-channel thalweg principle for determining the boundary.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to separate the positions of the two countries.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: Operation Meghdoot, associated with the Siachen dispute, was conducted in:
accepted.x: India secured the Siachen glacier through Operation Meghdoot in April 1984.
accepted.tq: Match the military operation with its year and geographical theatre.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: The dispute relating to Siachen primarily concerns the unmarked line beyond:
accepted.x: The Siachen dispute concerns the unmarked line beyond point NJ9842.
accepted.tq: Test precise location-based recall rather than the broader name of the glacier.
accepted.sec: Composite dialogue - baskets, backchannel, Sir Creek, Siachen  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on:
accepted.x: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, after the tribal invasion. Indian troops were airlifted on 27 October.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of accession from the following day on which troops were airlifted.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s:
The Instrument of Accession signed by Maharaja Hari Singh ceded which of the following subjects to India?
1. Defence
2. External affairs
3. Communications
4. Land revenue
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Instrument of Accession ceded only defence, external affairs and communications. Land revenue was not among the subjects specified in the material.
accepted.tq: Use the word 'only' to identify the limited scope of the accession.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: India took the Kashmir issue to the United Nations Security Council in January 1948 under which provision of the UN Charter?
accepted.x: India brought the matter before the UNSC in January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.
accepted.tq: Test precise article-number recall in an international-relations context.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the United Nations position on Kashmir:
1. The proposed plebiscite was conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal.
2. The withdrawal required for holding the plebiscite never took place.
3. UNSC Resolution 47 was adopted in 1948 in this context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The UN call for a plebiscite was conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal, which never occurred, and UNSC Resolution 47 was adopted in 1948 in relation to the issue.
accepted.tq: Test the condition, its non-fulfilment and the associated resolution together.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: The 1949 ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir was renamed the Line of Control under the:
accepted.x: The 1949 ceasefire line was renamed the Line of Control under the Simla Agreement of 1972.
accepted.tq: Identify the agreement responsible for the change in terminology.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: Article 370 became operative in Jammu and Kashmir on:
accepted.x: Article 370 became operative on 17 November 1952. It was abrogated on 5 August 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commencement date from the later abrogation date.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act — Created the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh
UNSC Resolution 47 — Renamed the ceasefire line as the Line of Control
Simla Agreement — Established the Instrument of Accession
accepted.x: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 created the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Article 370 was abrogated on 5 August 2019, while the Simla Agreement renamed the ceasefire line as the LoC.
accepted.tq: Check whether the legal instrument is matched with its actual consequence.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: The Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of Article 370 in:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of Article 370 in December 2023.
accepted.tq: Use the direct date-recall method for a constitutional development.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a response adopted by Pakistan after the abrogation of Article 370?
o: Recognising the Line of Control as an international boundary
Raising the issue at the United Nations
accepted.x: Pakistan downgraded diplomatic ties, suspended bilateral trade and raised the issue at the UN; it also suspended the Samjhauta Express. It did not recognise the LoC as an international boundary.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated diplomatic response.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s: India's position regarding Gilgit-Baltistan is that it is:
o: An independent buffer territory outside Jammu and Kashmir
A demilitarised zone created by the Simla Agreement
A disputed maritime zone in the Rann of Kutch
accepted.x: India claims Gilgit-Baltistan as part of Jammu and Kashmir. The issue is described as one of political status, not a border dispute.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a political-status claim from a conventional border dispute.
accepted.sec: Kashmir issue - Instrument of Accession, UN, LoC, Article 370

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Mumbai 26/11 attacks
B. Parliament attack
C. Uri attack
D. Pulwama attack
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Parliament attack occurred in 2001, Mumbai 26/11 in 2008, Uri in 2016 and Pulwama in 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then arrange the remaining attacks by year.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Parliament attack of 13 December 2001 was followed by Operation Parakram, involving troop mobilisation. The Balakot airstrike followed Pulwama, while the Composite Dialogue was suspended after Mumbai 26/11.
accepted.tq: Match each attack with the immediate Indian response rather than with another event.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Uri attack occurred in September 2016.
2. India responded with surgical strikes across the Line of Control on launchpads.
3. The attack was carried out by Pakistan-based militants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Uri attack occurred in September 2016, was attributed to Pakistan-based militants, and was followed by surgical strikes across the LoC on launchpads.
accepted.tq: Combine date, attribution and response to test the complete event profile.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s:
With reference to the Pulwama attack, consider the following statements:
1. It involved a CRPF convoy.
2. It occurred on 14 February 2019.
3. It was attributed to Jaish-e-Mohammed.
4. India withdrew the Most Favoured Nation status in response.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Pulwama attack targeted a CRPF convoy on 14 February 2019 and was attributed to Jaish-e-Mohammed. India responded with the Balakot airstrike and withdrawal of MFN status.
accepted.tq: Check all four linked details of an attack, including the diplomatic-economic response.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s: The Indian response associated with the Mumbai 26/11 attacks was the:
o: Withdrawal of the Instrument of Accession
accepted.x: The Composite Dialogue was suspended after the Mumbai 26/11 attacks of November 2008.
accepted.tq: Associate a major attack with its specific diplomatic consequence.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Pahalgam attack and the reported Indian response?
o: The attack occurred in September 2016, targeted an army camp, and led to Operation Parakram.
The attack occurred on 22 April 2025, killed 26 civilians, and was followed by Operation Sindoor and the holding of the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.
The attack occurred on 14 February 2019, killed CRPF personnel, and was followed by the Balakot airstrike.
The attack occurred in November 2008, killed civilians in Mumbai, and led to suspension of the Composite Dialogue.
accepted.x: The Pahalgam attack occurred on 22 April 2025 and resulted in the killing of 26 civilians. The stated response was Operation Sindoor, involving strikes on terror targets inside Pakistan, along with keeping the IWT in abeyance.
accepted.tq: Use the event-response pair to eliminate options that belong to other attacks.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s: India's stated policy towards cross-border terrorism is best expressed by which of the following?
o: Zero tolerance for terrorism, with acts of terror having consequences
Acceptance of terrorism as a normal instrument of diplomacy
accepted.x: India's stated line is zero tolerance for terrorism, and acts of terror will have consequences.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated policy principle to identify the precise official position.
accepted.sec: Cross-border terrorism - major attacks and India's responses

accepted.s: The UNSC 1267 sanctions committee is associated with sanctions against:
o: Countries breaching World Trade Organization rules
ISIL and Al-Qaida-related terrorists and entities
accepted.x: The UNSC 1267 committee deals with ISIL/Al-Qaida sanctions and lists terrorists and entities for asset freezes and travel bans.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution by its subject area and sanctioning function.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s:
Which of the following sanctions are associated with listing by the UNSC 1267 committee?
1. Asset freezes
2. Travel bans
3. Automatic military intervention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The committee's listing regime includes asset freezes and travel bans. Listing does not automatically entail military intervention.
accepted.tq: Reject the exaggerated consequence while retaining the two specified sanctions.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s: Masood Azhar was listed by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee in May 2019 after:
accepted.x: Masood Azhar, the chief of Jaish-e-Mohammed, was listed in May 2019 after China lifted its technical hold.
accepted.tq: Test the diplomatic trigger associated with an international terror listing.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hafiz Saeed — Listed in May 2019 after China's technical hold
FATF grey list — Pakistan removed in June 2018
accepted.x: Hafiz Saeed of LeT/JuD was listed in 2008. Masood Azhar was listed in May 2019 after China lifted its technical hold, and Pakistan was removed from the FATF grey list in October 2022.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two terrorist leaders and their different listing dates.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s: Pakistan remained on the FATF grey list from:
accepted.x: Pakistan was under increased monitoring on the FATF grey list from June 2018 until its removal in October 2022.
accepted.tq: Recall both endpoints of a period rather than only the year of removal.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s: FATF pressure is used by India primarily as a lever against:
accepted.x: India uses FATF pressure as a lever concerning terror financing.
accepted.tq: Connect the institution's monitoring mechanism with its policy relevance.
accepted.sec: Terror listings - UNSC 1267 committee, FATF grey list

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indus Waters Treaty and India's current position:
1. The Treaty is presently in abeyance.
2. India has rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling referred to in the current discussion.
3. India is seeking to renegotiate the Treaty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Treaty remains in abeyance, India has rejected the stated PCA ruling, and India is seeking to renegotiate the Treaty.
accepted.tq: Test the present status, response and policy direction as three separate propositions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states India's position regarding third-party mediation in India-Pakistan disputes?
o: India accepts mediation only in water-related disputes.
India supports mandatory mediation by the United Nations in every dispute.
India favours mediation by a group of neighbouring countries.
India maintains Simla-based bilateralism and rejects third-party mediation.
accepted.x: Simla-based bilateralism, meaning resolution through bilateral mechanisms without third-party mediation, remains India's fixed position.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise diplomatic principle and reject broader or conditional formulations.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
With reference to criticisms of the Indus Waters Treaty, consider the following statements:
1. The Treaty gives India about 20% of the waters.
2. The Treaty contains an aquifer clause.
3. The Treaty contains a drought clause.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Treaty gives India about 20% of the waters and is criticised for having neither an aquifer clause nor a drought clause.
accepted.tq: Use the absence of provisions to defeat the two falsely asserted clauses.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The 2025 holding of the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance was significant because it was described as the:
o: First suspension of the Treaty since 1960
First suspension of the Treaty since 1984
First amendment of the Treaty since 1972
First termination of the Treaty since 1947
accepted.x: The 2025 abeyance was described as the first suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty since it was concluded in 1960.
accepted.tq: Use the first-since construction to identify the correct historical benchmark.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
